core_obligations: Note that an isomorphism over R_p descends to some R_f because R_p = colim R_f, quoting the Algebra colimit statement (proof lines 19644-19647).
Reduce to the case where R is local and p is the maximal ideal (proof line 19648).
In the local case, apply the uniqueness of a minimal complex representing a perfect object, quoted as the lifting-from-the-residue-field statement (proof lines 19649-19651).
Use the fact that any complex is a direct sum of a trivial complex and a minimal one, quoted from the Algebra chapter, to conclude (proof lines 19652-19653).
difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a ring R, a prime p, and bounded complexes M^bullet and N^bullet of finite projective R-modules representing the same object of D(R), and asserts that there is f not in p and an isomorphism of complexes M^bullet_f oplus P^bullet = N^bullet_f oplus Q^bullet, where P^bullet and Q^bullet are finite direct sums of trivial complexes of the form ... -> 0 -> R_f -> R_f -> 0 -> ... placed in arbitrary degrees (source lines 19627-19641). The proof first localizes: if an isomorphism of the described type exists over R_p, then since R_p = colim R_f one can descend it to R_f for some f (proof lines 19644-19647). This reduces to the case where R is local and p is the maximal ideal (proof lines 19648-19648). In that case the result follows from the uniqueness of a minimal complex representing a perfect object, quoted as the lifting-from-the-residue-field statement, together with the fact that any complex is a direct sum of a trivial complex and a minimal one, quoted from the Algebra chapter (proof lines 19649-19653). The non-routine content is entirely in the reduction step: the localization argument converts a statement invoked at a prime into an isomorphism that exists on a Zariski neighbourhood, and the local case itself is delegated to the minimal-complex uniqueness theorem.
